title: Keep the Fairness
statementMd:
There are $n$ teams and $m$ distinct souvenirs. The teams are numbered from $1$ to $n$, and the souvenirs are numbered from $1$ to $m$.

Each team ranks all souvenirs from most preferred to least preferred. The ranking of team $i$ is a permutation [ t_{i,1},t_{i,2},...,t_{i,m}, ] where $t_{i,1}$ is its most preferred souvenir.

Every souvenir has already been assigned to exactly one team. Let $a_k$ be the team to which souvenir $k$ is assigned. A team may receive any number of souvenirs, including none.

The assignment is called **prefix-fair** if the following condition holds:

- For every team $i$, every other team $j$, and every integer $L$ with $1\le L\le m$, among the first $L$ souvenirs in team $i$'s ranking, the number assigned to team $i$ is at least the number assigned to team $j$.

Both numbers in this comparison are counted using team $i$'s ranking. Equality is allowed.

Determine whether the given assignment is prefix-fair.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $n$ and $m$ ($1\le n,m\le 2000$), the number of teams and the number of souvenirs.

The next $n$ lines describe the rankings. The $i$-th of these lines contains $m$ pairwise distinct integers $t_{i,1},t_{i,2},\dots,t_{i,m}$ ($1\le t_{i,k}\le m$), from team $i$'s most preferred souvenir to its least preferred souvenir. Thus, each line is a permutation of $1,2,\dots,m$.

The last line contains $m$ integers $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_m$ ($1\le a_k\le n$), where $a_k$ is the team to which souvenir $k$ is assigned.

## Output

Print one line containing `YES` if the assignment is prefix-fair. Otherwise, print `NO`.

The answer is case-sensitive.

## Note

In the first example, consider team $2$. The owners of the souvenirs in its ranking are [ 2,1,3,2,1,3. ] In every prefix, team $2$ occurs at least as many times as each of team $1$ and team $3$. The same property holds for teams $1$ and $3$, so the assignment is prefix-fair.

In the second example, the first three souvenirs in team $1$'s ranking are $1,2,4$. Team $1$ receives only souvenir $1$, while team $2$ receives souvenirs $2$ and $4$. Therefore, this prefix contains one souvenir assigned to team $1$ and two assigned to team $2$, so the assignment is not prefix-fair. Notice that both teams still receive two souvenirs in total; equal total numbers alone are not sufficient.
